bottom_line_fact.text: TrendForce projects conventional DRAM contract prices rising 10–15% QoQ and NAND Flash 15–20% QoQ in 4Q26, with server DRAM remaining undersupplied as suppliers prioritize advanced-process capacity for high-performance server products.

bottom_line_inference.text: Sustained AI server demand and supplier capacity reallocation toward server products support a continued memory up-cycle into 4Q26, though the pace of DRAM price gains is moderating.

disconfirming_observables: Server CPU/memory supply fully catching up to demand
DRAM or NAND contract prices undershooting the 10–15% / 15–20% QoQ ranges
Weak consumer demand dragging blended pricing lower

near_term_view.text: DRAM +10–15% QoQ and NAND +15–20% QoQ projected for 4Q26, with server DRAM undersupplied.

market_risks.scope_qualification: Applies to consumer-facing memory segments (PC DRAM, mobile DRAM, client SSD, eMMC/UFS, NAND wafer); does not negate AI-driven server/enterprise strength.
market_risks.statement: Consumer-side memory demand remains weak — PC DRAM end-market sales pressured by higher component costs, mobile/smartphone bit demand suppressed, client SSD procurement limited by inventories, and eMMC/UFS and NAND wafer buyers cautious — which could restrain blended pricing despite AI strength.

market_risks.scope_qualification: Supplier-specific; applies to DRAM suppliers bound by LTAs.
market_risks.statement: Some suppliers' price increases are expected to lag the market average in 4Q26 due to pricing mechanisms stipulated in long-term agreements, diluting realized price gains.
